title: The eventual non-ℓ-distance-balance conjecture for generalized Petersen graphs
source: Štefko Miklavič and Primož Šparl, “ℓ-distance-balanced graphs”, arXiv:1702.05257 (2017), Conjecture 4.4. https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.05257

significance.root_decision: For every k ≥ 2 and n > n_k, GP(n,k) is connected and is not ℓ-distance-balanced for any 1 ≤ ℓ < D; at n = n_k some 1 ≤ ℓ < D is balanced, so n_k is the least threshold. Published work covers only k = 3, 4 (arXiv:2309.01900) and distance 1 with weaker distance-2 bounds (Ma, Wang and Klavžar, arXiv:2407.02635). The proof gives an explicit distance formula for GP(n,k) with n ≥ k(k+2), uses the rotation and reflection automorphisms to cancel the common layer-distance profiles of a pair at distance ℓ, and reduces |W_xy| − |W_yx| to sparse 'axis pulses' whose sum is shown to be nonzero for every 1 ≤ ℓ < D by explicit witnesses; k = 2 and the sharpness at n_k are handled by finite certificates and explicit balanced distances. Lean defines GP(n,k) on Bool × ZMod n with Mathlib's SimpleGraph, W_xy as the vertices strictly closer to x, and proves connectivity for all n > n_k so that the diameter condition cannot hold vacuously.
significance.caveat: The journal text of the source could not be read and the census of citing papers is incomplete. The Lean proof is long (77 modules, 5,623 lines over four stages). Cross-model confidence 0.70, not routine 0.75. No second cross-model lane read the finished Lean: root compared the final theorem and every definition with the endpoint the Claude Opus reviewer had written (identical), and the GPT-6.1 Sol final check compared the definitions with the source and ran 55 independent breadth-first checks (k = 2 to 6, n from n_k to n_k + 10) and 54,831 arithmetic checks.
